parsed.explanation: The combined regime rests on a criminal statute in force with custodial penalties (sections 430/431, plus a gender-neutral indecency provision) that a single 2023 government report says is not enforced. Trans-specific exposure is not documented: no border, custody, facility or violence record for trans people, and no enforcement data. The structural gaps are real. Birth-sex documents cannot be amended, there is no anti-discrimination or harassment recourse, and fear of prosecution deters reporting to police, which affects visitors too. Documented discrimination in services is local-sphere and lacks a geographic breakdown. The 2013 repeal call is stale. Thin-data extrapolation from criminalisation, no recognition and no recourse places the rating in the Elevated band, not the midpoint, and the non-enforcement finding keeps it above High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport carries birth-sex or foreign-issued marker; no domestic amendment route, so marker mismatch is possible for any trans visitor.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch at entry could raise questioning; the dossier does not show how officers treat such documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Criminalising sections remain in force with up to ten years' custody; the 2023 report says they are not enforced. No custody or detention data for trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Non-enforcement reported for 2023 by one government source only.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If a document or presentation issue triggered police contact, the statute could be read against a trans visitor; no documented pathway.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation documented; island-wide provider and national frame apply.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Single national regime; no state-level layer to assess.

care_services.exposure: No information on hormone therapy or trans-specific care; sources name only one local service provider serving LGBTIQ+ and other groups.
care_services.interaction: Unknown whether care access is denied on discovery; open question.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Discrimination in public services documented; fear of prosecution deters police reporting; no official trans-targeting documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No constitutional equality or privacy clause; no anti-discrimination or harassment law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Absence of recourse combined with deterred reporting means a visitor harmed by anyone has little route to remedy.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific rule documented; no trans-specific custody or school rule for visitors. Education discrimination is documented for residents.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a minor would have no documented shield; birth-sex documents may complicate travel with a minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence documented; 2023 report records no arbitrary killings, torture or disappearances. Sources mention harassment and violence against LGBTIQ people generally.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented hate-crime or harassment recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting is deterred by fear of prosecution, so street violence may go unreported and unremedied.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No remedy for discrimination; no marker-amendment route; no unions or spousal recognition, so a trans visitor with a same-sex-read partner has no spousal protections.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A 2013 public call for repeal produced no legislation; advocacy has not produced change.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Reform advocacy does not operate as protection for visitors.

anchor_checks.comparison: Anchor 0.35-A has an active, universal entry exclusion register that refuses trans visitors on sight, and this dossier documents no such border practice. The case is higher than 0.35-A because the statute is not enforced and no exclusion is documented. It is similar to 0.35-A only in the absence of recourse.

Anchor 0.45-B has documented enforcement against visitors in schools and clinics, with delegated restrictions and limited remedy. This dossier has no documented service-denial or institutional exclusion of trans people, so it is roughly comparable in unremedied exposure but less concrete, which places it near 0.45.

Anchor 0.55-D has documented bureaucratic document mismatches that repeatedly delay and expose trans visitors. This dossier documents the birth-sex marker and no amendment route, so the mismatch is structural, but the dossier does not show it operating at the border. The case sits slightly below 0.55-D for lack of documented operation, and it is rated lower because of the in-force custodial statute.

parsed.synthesis: The statute is in force with custodial penalties, but the only enforcement signal is a single report saying it is not enforced. No trans-specific border, custody, facility or violence record is documented. The operative exposures are structural and unremedied: birth-sex documents with no amendment route, no anti-discrimination or harassment recourse, documented discrimination in public services, and fear of prosecution deterring reports to police. Those gaps apply to visitors as well as residents. There is no documented shield, care protection or working remedy to offset them, so the rating reflects Elevated Risk resolved from structural signals rather than a midpoint.
